blogs.title: Unlocking 1.58‑Bit LLMs: How Ternary Weights Give Transformers a Performance Boost
blogs.description: In this post we explain BitNet b1.58’s core idea—every weight is one of –1, 0, or +1. We’ll explore why adding a zero value strengthens feature filtering, demystify the absmean quantization process, and show how such a minimalistic representation still rivals full‑precision models in perplexity and real‑world tasks.

blogs.title: Speed, Memory, and Energy in a Nutshell: The Practical Gains of 1.58‑Bit LLMs
blogs.description: Discover how integer‑only matrix multiplication and 8‑bit activations slash inference latency, GPU memory, and energy draw. We’ll walk through the performance curves—up to 4× faster and 3× lighter than FP16—and discuss why these savings matter for cloud data centers, edge inference, and everyday AI services.

blogs.title: New Scaling Laws for Language Models: What 1.58‑Bit LLMs Teach Us About Size and Cost
blogs.description: BitNet b1.58 introduces a fresh scaling law that equates and even outperforms full‑precision models at lower compute. We’ll illustrate the equivalence chart (e.g., 13‑B 1.58‑bit beats 3‑B FP16) and explain how researchers can use these insights to choose model size, compute budget, and deployment strategy.

blogs.title: Deploying LLMs on Your Phone: Making 1.58‑Bit Models Truly Edge‑Ready
blogs.description: Low‑bit weights drastically shrink memory footprints, reduce DRAM bandwidth, and lean CPU‑friendly integer math. This article investigates how 1.58‑bit LLMs enable on-device inference for chat apps, personal assistants, and privacy‑preserving queries, while outlining the remaining trade‑offs in recall and latency.

blogs.title: Hardware for 1.58‑Bit LLMs: The Next Generation of AI Accelerators
blogs.description: We look ahead at specialized chips—like Groq’s LPUs and future custom ASICs—that can exploit 1‑bit matrix multiplication without costly multipliers. Learn about on‑chip SRAM, SIMD routing, and energy‑efficient adder trees that make a dedicated 1.58‑bit accelerator a realistic win for large‑scale inference.

blogs.title: MoE Meets 1‑Bit: Lighter, Faster, and More Efficient Expert Models
blogs.description: Mixture‑of‑Experts already trims FLOPs, but memory and communication kill performance at scale. With 1.58‑bit weights, a MoE model’s memory footprint shrinks, enabling it to fit on fewer chips and eliminating cross‑chip activation traffic. We discuss how this combination could power massive‑scale generative AI with modest hardware.
